title: §09-001: Sequential Asynchronous Flow Control
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §09-001 (Sequential Asynchronous Flow Control).

cards.concept: Sequential Asynchronous Flow Control: Asynchronous Concurrency Limiting
cards.question: Why does unbounded `Promise.all(urls.map(fetch))` cause outages under high load, and how does concurrency pooling prevent it?

options.text: Promise.all forces all requests to run sequentially on the main thread.
Firing thousands of concurrent network requests exhausts operating system file descriptors and socket pools, leading to ECONNRESET and memory spikes.
V8 garbage collection automatically cancels promises if more than 100 are active.
HTTP/1.1 servers crash if more than 2 requests arrive concurrently.

cards.explanation: Unbounded Promise.all spawns concurrent requests without limits, exhausting sockets and system memory. A concurrency limiter restricts active concurrent tasks to a bounded pool (e.g. p-limit).
cards.pitfall: Failing to bound concurrency when fan-out querying a relational database, exhausting the database connection pool.
cards.citation: Node.js Production Best Practices: Concurrency Management

cards.concept: Sequential Asynchronous Flow Control: AbortController & Timeout Cancellation
cards.question: How should an engineer implement strict timeout boundaries on asynchronous fetch or stream operations in Node.js?

options.text: Use process.kill(process.pid) after a setTimeout.
Pass `AbortSignal.timeout(ms)` to the `signal` option of fetch or stream pipelines, which automatically aborts and cleans up resources upon expiry.
Wrap the function in a while loop checking Date.now().
Call process.abort() in a setTimeout callback.

cards.explanation: AbortSignal.timeout(ms) creates an AbortSignal that fires after a specified duration, closing underlying TCP sockets and rejecting with an AbortError without leaking resources.
cards.pitfall: Relying on Promise.race with a setTimeout without aborting the slower promise leaves the underlying network socket open in the background.
